name: Fusarium Head Blight
symptoms: Premature bleaching of cereal heads One or more spikelets turn white while the rest remain green Pink or orange fungal spores at the base of glumes Whitish or pink fluffy fungal growth on infected heads in wet weather Shriveled, lightweight and bleached kernels (tombstone kernels)
description: A serious fungal disease of cereal crops that infects the heads of plants such as wheat and barley. It reduces grain yield and quality and can produce a toxic compound (mycotoxin) in the grain.
management: Use resistant or tolerant cereal varieties Rotate crops and avoid planting cereals after corn Use clean certified seeds Apply seed treatment before planting Scout fields during flowering for symptoms Harvest early when infection risk is high Dry and aerate grain properly during storage
prevention: Rotate crops for at least 2 years with non-host crops Manage crop residues by tillage or decomposition Avoid highly susceptible varieties Use proper irrigation management during flowering Separate and test contaminated grain before feeding livestock
